newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to firm, helped by weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to firm, helped by weaker yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to firm in the Tuesday session, carrying over positive sentiment from the previous session backed by a weakening yen, brokers said.
They said that global issues would lead the market, helped by another record high on Wall Street and strength in Nikkei futures in Chicago overnight.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average closed up 185.72 points or 0.91 percent at 20,575.26, after briefly rising as high as 20,600.66.

"The near-term target for the Nikkei average is the 1997 closing high of 20,681 reached on June 16," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager, said. "Gains above that level can only be achieved, however, if buying interest spreads to issues other than blue chips and if turnover picks up."
Brokers said that a climb in Sony Corp's American Depositary Receipts to a 12-month high on Monday in New York would be encouraging for investors.
